A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CommonSyn research. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison, including material moved between the appendices and main text.

before.justification: v1 reports original fine-tuning experiments across 11 models, downstream evaluations, selection ablations, dataset-scaling results, and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds PersonaHub baseline results and a human evaluation of agreement with GPT-4o.

M1.justification: Section 3.4 changes the specified global ranking score from raw Q plus global diversity to the sum of their min-max-normalized values, affecting their relative weighting. The remaining generation and selection pipeline is retained. The PDFs do not establish whether existing experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: v2 adds persona-conditioned synthetic concept sets and sentences for training the PersonaHub baseline (Section 4.4). The existing CommonSyn/CommonGen data and CommonGen, ComVE, alpha-NLG, ROCStories, CSQA, CSQA2, and PIQA evaluation coverage are retained.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds an evaluated PersonaHub baseline alongside CommonGen and Prismatic. PersonaHub's underlying work was already cited in v1, but its experimental comparison is new. Existing comparator memberships are otherwise retained.

E3.justification: v2 introduces human evaluation on 50 randomly sampled examples using the same instructions as the LLM evaluator (Appendix E). The existing models, LoRA settings, temperatures, metrics, and evaluation prompts remain unchanged; most implementation settings were already documented in v1 Appendix A.

E4.justification: The new human-rating analysis tests whether GPT-4o judgments agree with human judgments. Existing concept-construction and selection ablations, concept-set scaling analysis, and qualitative case studies are retained without substantive changes.

E5.justification: v2 newly reports human–GPT-4o percentage agreement and Cohen's kappa as evaluator-reliability statistics. The existing bootstrap significance reporting remains unchanged, with no added repeated-run counts, seed information, or confidence intervals.

E6.justification: Table 3 adds PersonaHub results, including Win-Tie 20.8, Overall 19.6, and S-Cos 35.6. Appendix E adds 81.6% human–GPT-4o agreement and kappa 0.648. Retained benchmark, ablation, scaling, and case-study results are unchanged after matching relocated tables and equivalent numerical formatting.

T1.justification: Equation 3 substantively revises the score definition through min-max normalization. Equation 2 expresses the existing average cosine-diversity score equivalently using a sum of unit-normalized embeddings; that reformulation does not itself introduce a different mathematical criterion. No theorems or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the same central claims: a synthetic dataset for diversified commonsense reasoning, two-stage selection, quality–diversity improvements across 11 models, and downstream generalization. The expanded conclusion summarizes existing claims about scale, coverage, and generalization.

C2.justification: v2 attributes PersonaHub's lower plausibility to persona-driven role-playing outputs. Section 6 adds specific discussion of verbosity and self-enhancement biases, explaining existing evaluator choices as mitigations. Appendix E interprets the new human agreement results as supporting evaluator reliability.

D1.justification: The first-page footnote replaces a release-on-acceptance promise with a code/data access link. v2 also describes PersonaHub data generation and clarifies equal sample counts in selection comparisons. Moving implementation details into Section 4.1 does not newly disclose the existing hardware and fine-tuning settings.

R1.justification: v2 adds Zheng et al. (2023), Shi et al. (2025), and Wang et al. (2024) to support discussion of LLM-judge biases. It also expands comparison with the already-cited PersonaHub work. The broader related-work organization and novelty positioning remain stable.

P1.justification: Implementation Details moves from v1 Appendix A to v2 Section 4.1, with corresponding renumbering. v2 makes localized language corrections, expands the conclusion, updates affiliations, and adds acknowledgements. Most prose and the overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: Table 3 gains the PersonaHub row, and result tables update boldface emphasis. The training-prompt table moves into the main text, while the full-results table moves ahead of the appendix prompt figures. Figures and existing table content are retained, with limited caption and layout adjustments.

improvement.justification: The added PersonaHub comparison and 50-example human validation modestly strengthen the evidence, while the access link, score specification, and table emphasis improve reporting. Benefits remain limited: existing benchmark results are unchanged, human-rater details are sparse, and Section 6 retains a pairwise-computation bottleneck discussion despite Equation 2's aggregate-vector formulation.
